recycle-code-pet.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 1 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 1, PET or PETE, the plastic in drinks bottles and food trays.

recycle-code-hdpe.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 2 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 2, HDPE, the plastic in milk jugs, detergent bottles and pipes.

recycle-code-pvc.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 3 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 3, PVC, the plastic in pipes, cling wrap and window frames.

recycle-code-ldpe.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 4 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 4, LDPE, the soft plastic in carrier bags and squeezable bottles.

recycle-code-pp.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 5 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 5, polypropylene, the plastic in yoghurt tubs, bottle caps and straws.

recycle-code-ps.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 6 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 6, polystyrene, the plastic in foam cups, packing peanuts and takeaway trays.

recycle-code-other.context: A triangle of three chasing arrows with the number 7 inside. Stamped on plastic goods to show resin type 7, other or mixed plastics, such as polycarbonate and bioplastics.

glass-recycling.context: A tall recycling bank with a round opening and a bottle shape on its front. Marks bottle banks and bins for glass jars and bottles.

paper-recycling.context: A recycling bin with a slot opening and a folded newspaper on its front. Used for paper and cardboard collection points and sorting guides.

metal-recycling.context: A recycling bank with a round opening and a tin can on its front. Marks bins for drinks cans, tins and scrap metal.

plastic-recycling.context: A wheeled recycling bin with a lid and a plastic bottle on its front. Marks bins and sorting guides for plastic bottles and packaging.

battery-recycling.context: A battery inside a loop of two chasing arrows. Used for battery drop-off points and guidance on safe disposal of used cells.

e-waste-recycling.context: A smartphone inside a loop of two chasing arrows. Stands for electronic waste recycling, device take-back and refurbishing.

textile-recycling.context: A t-shirt inside a loop of two chasing arrows. Used for clothing recycling, fabric waste collection and reuse of worn garments.

clothing-donation-bin.context: A tall clothing collection container with a sloped roof, a dividing line and a shirt mark on its front. Seen at charity drop-off points.

reverse-vending-machine.context: A bottle being pushed into the slot of an upright return machine that has a receipt slot below. Used for deposit refund kiosks in shops.

deposit-return.context: A bottle beside a coin and a circular arrow. Shows bottle deposit schemes where containers are returned for a refund.

food-waste.context: An apple core with a stem sitting in a small bin. Stands for kitchen scraps, leftovers and food waste reduction or collection.

zero-waste.context: A glass jar with a lid and a zero on its front. Represents the zero waste lifestyle, refill shopping and waste-free living.

reusable-bag.context: A cloth tote bag with two long handles and a leaf printed on it. Used for eco shopping, plastic bag alternatives and bag-for-life schemes.

reusable-cup.context: A takeaway cup with a sip lid and a sleeve band. Used for bring-your-own coffee cup schemes and waste-free drinks.

bamboo-toothbrush.context: A toothbrush turned on the diagonal with a row of bristles and a handle marked with bamboo joints. A plastic-free dental care product.

beeswax-wrap.context: A square cloth wrap with a folded corner, printed with a small honeycomb of hexagons. A reusable alternative to cling film.

bulk-food-jars.context: Two wide glass jars with lids and fill lines. Used for bulk buying, refill shops, dry goods storage and package-free pantries.

metal-straw.context: A bent drinking straw standing beside a thin cleaning brush. A reusable alternative to single-use plastic straws.

upcycling.context: A tin can used as a plant pot, with a sprout growing out of it. Stands for reusing objects in a new way and craft repurposing.

secondhand.context: A clothes hanger inside a circular arrow loop. Marks thrift stores, preloved clothing and resale of used goods.

circular-economy.context: Three curved arrows forming a closed circle around a leaf. Stands for the circular economy, closed-loop production and regeneration.

repair-cafe.context: A coffee mug holding a wrench and a pin, like tools in a pot. Stands for community repair events where people fix things together.

biodegradable.context: A leaf above a dotted arrow pointing down to the ground. Means a material that breaks down naturally into soil.

compostable-packaging.context: A takeaway box with a sprout growing from its top. Labels packaging made from plant material that can be composted.

eco-label.context: A scalloped seal badge with a leaf in its center. Used for environmental certification marks and green product approval.

sustainable-packaging.context: A cardboard box with a leaf printed on its side. Stands for recyclable, plastic-free and low-impact packaging.

street-litter-bin.context: A public bin on a post with a wide lid and a slot opening. Used on city streets and in parks for rubbish collection.

solar-farm.context: Two rows of tilted solar panels on open ground with a small sun in the corner. Stands for large solar power plants.

solar-charger.context: A folding solar panel connected by a cable to a smartphone. Used for portable solar charging, camping and travel power.

solar-street-light.context: A street lamp post with a lamp head and a small tilted solar panel on top. Used for off-grid outdoor lighting.

solar-roof.context: A house roof triangle covered with grid lines and a base line. Stands for rooftop solar panels and home solar power.

small-wind-turbine.context: A short three-blade wind turbine on a pole beside a house. Stands for domestic and small-scale wind power.

micro-hydro.context: A pipe running down a slope into a turbine box marked with a bolt. Stands for small stream-fed hydroelectric power.

biomass.context: A pile of three log ends beside a small flame. Stands for wood fuel, pellets and heat or power from organic material.

renewable-energy.context: A large leaf with a lightning bolt in the middle. Stands for green electricity and clean power from natural sources.

green-hydrogen.context: A leaf beside a gas cylinder marked with the letter H. Stands for hydrogen fuel made with renewable electricity.

micro-grid.context: Three small houses joined by lines in a triangle. Stands for local power networks that share energy between buildings.

smart-grid.context: A power pylon with linked network dots around it. Stands for digitally connected electricity networks and smart metering.

off-grid-cabin.context: A small cabin with a solar panel on its roof beside a wind turbine. Stands for self-sufficient living away from the mains.

energy-efficiency-label.context: Four stepped bars that shorten from top to bottom. Stands for appliance and building energy rating scales.

home-insulation.context: A house section with a zigzag insulation layer inside its walls. Stands for loft, wall and roof insulation upgrades.

draft-excluder.context: A door with a long stuffed tube lying along its bottom edge. Stops cold air coming under doors.

energy-audit.context: A clipboard with a lightning bolt and a line of text. Stands for home energy assessments and efficiency surveys.

energy-monitor.context: A small display unit showing a bar graph and a bolt. Stands for in-home electricity usage monitors.

standby-power.context: A power button symbol beside a small crescent moon. Stands for phantom load and devices left on standby.

low-flow-shower.context: A shower head with only three thin lines of water. Stands for water-saving showers and efficient fixtures.

dual-flush-toilet.context: A toilet tank lid with one large round button and one small round button. Stands for water-saving flush choices.

passive-house.context: A house outline with a large window and a sun shining toward it. Stands for very low energy homes that use solar gain.

green-building.context: A stepped office tower with window dots and small leaves growing from its sides. Stands for sustainable architecture.

bike-commute.context: A bicycle with a briefcase strapped above its rear wheel. Stands for cycling to work and low-carbon commuting.

walking-commute.context: A person walking beside a leaf. Stands for walking to work or school as a low-carbon way to travel.

eco-house.context: A house outline with a leaf growing where the chimney would be. Stands for green, energy-efficient homes.

green-city.context: City buildings with a tree between them and a leaf above. Stands for urban greening and sustainable city planning.

urban-farm.context: An apartment building with a row of young plants growing on its roof. Stands for rooftop farms and city agriculture.

community-garden.context: A raised garden bed with young plants and a person standing beside it. Stands for shared neighborhood growing spaces.

allotment.context: A picket fence around a small plot with young plants and a garden shed. Stands for rented vegetable growing plots.

plant-based-diet.context: A round plate holding a leaf and a carrot. Stands for vegan and vegetarian eating and meat-free meals.

local-produce.context: A basket with a map pin above it. Stands for locally grown food, farmers markets and short supply chains.

organic-label.context: A round seal with a check mark whose end sprouts a leaf. Stands for certified organic food and natural products.

endangered-species.context: A rhinoceros head in profile with horns, inside a circle. Stands for threatened animals and conservation status lists.

wildlife-protection.context: A shield with a deer head and antlers inside. Stands for wildlife conservation and protected habitats.

nature-reserve.context: A direction signpost beside a tree with a bird flying above. Stands for protected natural areas and park trails.

tree-nursery.context: A bench holding a row of young potted saplings. Stands for growing young trees and plants for planting out.

seed-bank.context: A square vault door with a round wheel and a seed in its center. Stands for seed storage and crop diversity.

bee-hotel.context: A wooden insect house with a pitched roof and rows of round nesting holes. Gives solitary bees a place to nest.

pollinator-garden.context: A flower on a stem with a bee hovering beside it. Stands for bee-friendly planting and wildflower gardens.
